subject: Chemistry
question: The mass spectrum of an unknown element is displayed below. The atomic mass of the unknown element is

image.alt: Mass spectrum of an unknown element showing isotopic peaks at m/z = 70, 75, and 78 with relative abundances of approximately 69%, 6%, and 19% respectively

explanation:
Atomic mass is the weighted average of all isotope masses:

Atomic mass = Σ(mass × abundance) / Σ(abundance)

From the graph:
m/z = 70 with abundance ≈ 69%
m/z = 75 with abundance ≈ 6%
m/z = 78 with abundance ≈ 19%

= [(70 × 69) + (75 × 6) + (78 × 19)] / (69 + 6 + 19)
= (4830 + 450 + 1482) / 94
= 6762 / 94
≈ 71.9 ≈ 72

Note: You cannot just pick the tallest peak (70) — that's only the most abundant isotope, not the average.

Since a significant fraction of the sample is heavier (75 and 78), the weighted average is approximately 72.

modelAnswer:
(i) Electronegativity: The tendency of an atom in a molecule to attract the shared pair of electrons towards itself.

(ii) ICl₄⁻: I central, 4 Cl bonded, 2 lone pairs (6 electron pairs) — square planar from octahedral electron geometry.

(i) Alcohol = propan-2-ol (positive iodoform test).
CH₃CH(OH)CH₃ + 4I₂ + 6NaOH → CHI₃↓ + CH₃COONa + 5NaI + 5H₂O.
Yellow precipitate = triiodomethane (iodoform, CHI₃).

(ii) CH₃−CH(OH)−CH₃.

(iii) Propanone (acetone, CH₃COCH₃).

subject: Chemistry
question:
(b) A hydrocarbon X contains 92.3% carbon by mass. The relative molecular mass of X is 78.0.
(i) Calculate the empirical formula of X.
(ii) Calculate the molecular formula of X.
modelAnswer:
(i) C = 92.3%, H = 7.7%.
C:H = 7.692:7.7 = 1:1.
Empirical formula = CH.

(ii) n = 78/13 = 6.
Molecular formula = C₆H₆ (benzene).

subject: Chemistry
question:
(c) (i) Draw the structures of the TWO geometrical isomers of 1,2-dibromoethene.
(ii) What feature of the double bond prevents isomer 1 from changing into isomer 2?
(iii) Provide the name and structure for any monosubstituted benzene compound.
modelAnswer:
(i) cis-1,2-dibromoethene: Br on same side of C=C.
trans-1,2-dibromoethene: Br on opposite sides of C=C.

(ii) Restricted rotation about the C=C double bond (due to the π bond).

(iii) Chlorobenzene (C₆H₅Cl).

subject: Chemistry
question:
(a) Hydrocarbons with high molecular mass are subjected to a process known as cracking.
(i) Define the term cracking.
(ii) What conditions are used for cracking?
(iii) Differentiate between cracking and reforming.
modelAnswer:
(i) Cracking: Breaking large hydrocarbon molecules into smaller, more useful molecules by breaking C-C bonds.

(ii) High temperature (400–700°C), high pressure, and often a catalyst (zeolites for catalytic cracking).

(iii) Cracking: Breaks large alkanes into smaller alkanes and alkenes.
Reforming: Rearranges hydrocarbon structure (straight-chain → branched/cyclic/aromatic) without necessarily changing molecular size.

subject: Chemistry
question:
(b) The following scheme shows some reactions of toluene.
Reactions:
I: Toluene → Compound W (oxidation)
II: Toluene → Compound X (nitration)
III: Toluene → Compound Y (side-chain oxidation)
IV: Compound Y → Compound Z (further oxidation)
(i) Suggest reagents and conditions for reactions I to IV.
(ii) Give the IUPAC name of W, Y and Z.
modelAnswer:
(i) I: Hot alkaline KMnO₄ then acidify.
II: Conc. HNO₃ + conc. H₂SO₄ at ~30°C.
III: Controlled KMnO₄ oxidation.
IV: PCC or acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ distillation.

(ii) W = Benzoic acid.
Y = Benzyl alcohol (phenylmethanol).
Z = Benzaldehyde (benzenecarbaldehyde).

subject: Chemistry
question:
(c) B is a saturated unbranched hydrocarbon compound. When treated with chlorine under free radical conditions it produces a mixture of chlorinated compounds including C, C₆H₁₃Cl₂. Dehydrochlorination of C produces D, C₆H₁₂. When D is oxidized by hot conc. KMnO₄, two compounds, CO₂ and a carboxylic acid are formed in equimolar amounts.
(i) Suggest reagent and condition for the conversion of C to D.
(ii) Suggest a structure for compound D.
(iii) Deduce the structure of compound B.
modelAnswer:
(i) Reflux with alcoholic KOH (elimination reaction).

(ii) D = hex-1-ene (CH₂=CHCH₂CH₂CH₂CH₃).

(iii) C = 1,2-dichlorohexane.
B = hexane (C₆H₁₄).
